note: Every BRx.y, NFR and story for this Unit, mapped to the file that implements or enforces it. Targets are workspace-relative paths so the mapping is checkable mechanically; `rationale` carries what the path alone does not say. Where a control was verified against the WRONG implementation it exists to catch, the rationale records which tests fired and which did not — that distinction is the evidence, because every defect listed passes a confirmatory test. The reverse section records five decisions with no upstream rule, including two test defects found and fixed during the build.

coverage.rationale: The lens is derived from Owner and Enrollment on every request. No role column exists on Account, asserted by test_the_lens_is_never_read_from_a_column, and no module-level cache exists, asserted by a scan that was verified to detect a dict, an lru_cache and a set.
An account gaining an Owner row has the teacher lens on its NEXT request. Verified to FAIL against an injected cross-request cache; that is its only job.
The mirror, and the more dangerous direction: losing the last Enrollment removes the student lens next request. Also verified to fail against the cache.
Two lookups in one request hit the database once; two requests hit it twice. The pair is what makes it a boundary rather than a cache.
Datastore-backed counters under a unique constraint with an atomic upsert. The two-worker test was verified to fail against a per-process dictionary.
3/hour and 5/day per number, 10/hour per IP prefix, checked BEFORE the gateway call. A breach is a ConflictError, never a TransientError.
Five-minute expiry, single use via consumed_at set in the checking transaction under FOR UPDATE, and the attempt ceiling that KILLS the code rather than only refusing the attempt.

HMAC under a server-held key. The not-reproducible-without-the-key test was verified to fail against bare SHA-256 while the stored-differs-from-transmitted test PASSED, which is why NFR9.5 states both halves.
Narrowest-first, with a refused scope releasing its own increment. Both accounting tests were verified to fail against global-first ordering while every threshold test passed.
A breach returns a temporary-unavailability message_key. Tests assert the refusal names no limit and never says 'invalid'.

Both branches issue the SAME statements: the unknown branch performs the equivalent INSERT inside a savepoint and rolls it back. Verified against both defect shapes, including the subtle one that hashes on both branches but writes on only one.
Profile.self_name and Enrollment.display_name in different tables with different writers. A test asserts neither column appears in the other table.
RLS ENABLED and FORCED on profile with a policy keyed on the session account. FORCE matters independently: without it the policy does not apply to the table owner, who runs the migration.
The meta-test runs first, enforced by both collection ordering and a package-level gate. Verified: with a correct policy and a superuser connection, a teacher reads the profile anyway.
Rotation with reuse detection invalidating the whole FAMILY. Verified: against an implementation invalidating only the presented token, exactly one of five transitions fails.
Refresh tokens stored hashed through the same chokepoint as the OTP; access-token expiry compared server-side against our own clock rather than the library default.
kid header with two valid verification keys, tested by signing under one and verifying after the active key changed.
response_code == 202 and nothing else. A test asserts a body carrying only `code` does NOT read as success, which is the parsing the most-installed client for this gateway uses.
urlparse scheme asserted at CONSTRUCTION, so a misconfigured deployment fails at startup rather than shipping the first OTP in cleartext. No TLS toggle is exposed, asserted by signature.
One attempt, no retry at any layer. A timeout is UNKNOWN, never FAILED. A test asserts no code maps to TransientError across the whole table.
The null adapter is the DEFAULT; a misspelt setting yields it. A partially configured real adapter refuses to start rather than falling back.
GSM-7 SEPTET counting, not len(): the extended set costs two, so a naive length check passes on a body needing two segments. The app hash is counted.
Owner and Enrollment created empty and never written, asserted over this Unit's own source because the violation WORKS.
No free-form string column but correlation_id, asserted structurally. The gateway's error_message is never logged, verified against an injected debug log that leaked the API key.
A committed script with a __main__ guard, never imported by application code, asserted by an AST walk over every module.
ONE statement carrying three booleans and both scoping ids. My first draft used follow-up selects and the query-count assertion caught it.
A query COUNT, never a duration: a wall-clock assertion is flaky and gets deleted the third time CI fails on it.
A correlation id per request, generated in middleware so every log line and audit row in the request can carry it.
HMAC rather than a work-factor hash, following the measurement that reversed this design: bcrypt buys hours against an attacker who gets there anyway; HMAC stops one holding only the database.
B1's inherited money-column assertion, discharged. VACUOUS on U3 (stated as its own test) and verified to fire on double precision and on an unconstrained numeric created by hand-written SQL.
The count is compared AFTER the atomic increment, so two workers racing on one window cannot both read a stale value.
A teacher signs in end to end over HTTP: issue, the rendered SMS body, verify, a working token pair.
A dormant account activates on first successful verify, which is how a student or guardian claims a record a teacher created without being invited.
Owner-private profile, probed adversarially by three routes: direct query, join and ORM traversal.
The seven controls, each verified against the wrong implementation rather than only the right one.
Role resolved per request, with the two mid-session tests that fail against a cache.
Western numerals in the Bangla bundle, verified to fire on a single Bangla-Indic digit.
Both bundles on screen one, with every English string asserted to have a Bangla counterpart.
No SMS read permission, asserted by parsing uses-permission elements. The allowlist is empty at this Bolt, stated as a number so a first permission is a diff against zero.

reverse.target: tests/gates/test_coverage_scope.py — no upstream rule. B2's explicit --cov list did not mention B3's five new packages, so the 80% floor passed at 95% while measuring NONE of this Bolt's code. It did not fail; it silently covered less. The list is now asserted against the packages on disk, and the omission was reproduced to confirm the gate fires.

android/src/test/.../AuthSurfaceRulesTest.kt — a test defect found in the writing. The AD_ID check matched the manifest's explanatory COMMENT, which names AD_ID in order to forbid it. A test failing on the warning against a thing, while saying nothing about the thing, is worse than none: the obvious fix is to delete the warning.

app/gateway/bulksmsbd.py — _VALIDATION_CODES was declared and never read, which is dead configuration claiming more coverage than it has. taxonomy_for_code now exposes the full C.4.4 map, kept separate from outcome_for_code because the two answer different questions: what to record, versus whether a retry is allowed.

app/authz/rls.py — set_config(..., true) scopes the account id to the TRANSACTION. A session-scoped set is connection-scoped, and connections are pooled, so the next request would inherit the previous account's id. It looks identical in every single-request test.
app/db/seed_skeleton.py at 0% line coverage, deliberately. BR6.3 forbids application code from importing it and a test asserts none does; covering it would mean importing it.
